problem:
A quadratic equation in the variable $x$ with real coefficients has a root $x=2+\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $5,$ find the equation. Write your answer in the form $a{x}^{2}+bx+c=0,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are real constants.

feedback.problem:
A quadratic equation with real coefficients has a complex root $x=\sqrt{2}+3\text{i}.$ Given that the coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ in the equation is $1,$ find the equation. Write your answer in the form $a{x}^{2}+bx+c=0,$ where $a,$ $b,$ and $c$ are real constants.

{{field-1}}$=0$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the quadratic equation has real coefficients and $x=\sqrt{2}+3\text{i}$ is a root, we know that its complex conjugate $x=\sqrt{2}-3\text{i}$ is also a root. Therefore, using the zero product property, we can write a quadratic equation with the required roots as follows:

$$
(x-(\sqrt{2}+3\text{i}))(x-(\sqrt{2}-3\text{i}))=0
$$

By expanding the parentheses, we can write the equation in standard form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-x(\sqrt{2}+3\text{i})-x(\sqrt{2}-3\text{i})+(\sqrt{2}+3\text{i})(\sqrt{2}-3\text{i}) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-\sqrt{2}x-\cancel{3x\text{i}}-\sqrt{2}x+\cancel{3x\text{i}}+2-9{\text{i}}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2\sqrt{2}\,x+2+9 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2\sqrt{2}\,x+11 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
